newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles airport passenger, cargo rose in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles airport passenger, cargo rose in 1996.

text.p: Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) posted 57.9 million passengers and nearly two million tons of cargo for 1996, maintaining its status as the West Coast hub for tourism and trade, officials said Thursday.

Statistics for 1996 showed a passenger count of 57,974,559 -- a 7.5 percent increase compared with 1995 figures. In addition, air cargo increased 7.7 percent to 1,895,754 tons, officials with the Los Angeles Department of Airports said.
"We're pleased, but not surprised, by this tremendous growth in passenger and cargo traffic," John Driscoll, executive director of the department, said in a statement.
"LAX has consistently seen an eight percent to nine percent increase in aviation activity in recent years, and forecasts show this demand will continue for the next 20 years," Driscoll added.

International passenger traffic rose 4.7 percent to 14,032,531, while domestic passenger traffic grew 8.5 percent to 43,942,028. Aircraft operations increased 4.3 percent to 763,866, the department of airports said.
At Ontario International Airport, also operated by the department, passenger traffic totaled 6,242,434, down 2.5 percent, while air cargo reached 437,139 tons, up 13 percent.
Aircraft movements at the Ontario airport were logged at 154,314, down 1.3 percent.

Palmdale Regional Airport in the Antelope Valley reported 18,279 passengers for 1996, down 10.1 percent. Air freight increased 24.2 percent to 4,995 pounds, and commercial airline flights remained constant at 3,796.
The number of takeoffs and landings at Van Nuys Airport, located in the San Fernando Valley, also remained constant with 1995's figure of 521,465, the department of airports said.
